<h4> Assistant Professor of Biostatistics, Albert Einstein College of Medicine </h4> 

<div class="row" style="display: flex; align-items: center; margin-bottom: 20px;">

<div class="col-md-4">

<img src="images/profile.jpg" alt="Angel Garcia de la Garza" style="width:100%; border-radius: 4px;"/>

</div>

<div class="col-md-8">

I'm an Assistant Professor in the [Division of Biostatistics, Department of Epidemiology](https://www.einsteinmed.edu/departments/epidemiology-population-health/) at [Albert Einstein College of Medicine](https://www.einsteinmed.edu), with a secondary appointment in the Saul R. Korey Department of Neurology. My research focuses on the analysis of high-dimensional and longitudinal data in neuroscience, neurology, and psychiatry, with a particular interest in Alzheimer's disease and related dementias, blood-based biomarkers, and digital/smartphone-based cognitive assessments in diverse aging populations.

I completed my B.A. in Mathematics at the [University of Pennsylvania](https://www.upenn.edu/) in 2015 and my Ph.D. in Biostatistics at [Columbia University Mailman School of Public Health](https://www.publichealth.columbia.edu) in 2022. My dissertation, advised by [Jeff Goldsmith](https://jeffgoldsmith.com), focused on dimension reduction methodology for functional data and machine learning applications to epidemiologic surveys. My current work as Principal Investigator on an NIH/NIA R03 award (R03AG095655) examines machine learning tools to integrate pen-and-paper and smartphone self-reported cognitive concerns as predictors of longitudinal Alzheimer's biomarkers.
